title: Continuity and atlas quotient topology for arbitrary algebraic stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, morphisms and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Here an algebraic stack is a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a representable smooth surjective scheme atlas; smoothness is tested on scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For an algebraic stack $\mathcal A$, let $|\mathcal A|$ be the set of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal A$ from fields [def-weil-field], where two representatives are equivalent when their pullbacks to a common field extension are 2-isomorphic. The topology defined by a smooth surjective scheme atlas is independent of the atlas: for every such $p:U\to\mathcal A$, the map $|p|:|U|\to|\mathcal A|$ is surjective and a subset $D\subseteq|\mathcal A|$ is closed if and only if $|p|^{-1}(D)$ is closed in $|U|$. Every morphism $a:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ of algebraic stacks induces a continuous map $|a|:|\mathcal A|\to|\mathcal B|$. On schemes and algebraic spaces these topologies agree with the usual Zariski and etale-atlas topologies, respectively.

source.place: Tag 04XL (lemma-topology-points); atlas point-surjectivity: Tag 04XI (lemma-characterize-surjective); compatibility with spaces and schemes: discussion following Tag 04XG (definition-points).

proof.text: Composition with a stack morphism preserves the equivalence of field-valued representatives: whisker the given isomorphism over their common field extension with that morphism. Thus the point maps are well defined, preserve composition, and turn 2-commutative squares into commutative squares of sets, by the fibre-groupoid conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For any atlas $p:U\to\mathcal A$, the surjectivity assertion in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] gives, for every field-valued object $x$ of $\mathcal A$, an extension of its field and an object of $U$ whose image is isomorphic to $x$ after extension. Hence $|p|$ is surjective. For schemes, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] factors every field map through the residue-field map of its image point. Consequently the field-class points of a scheme identify with its ordinary points: each representative is equivalent to that residue-field representative, and equivalent representatives have the same image point. This identification is the one in [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes].

source.place: Tag 04XG (definition-points), following discussion; Tag 04XI (lemma-characterize-surjective), reverse implication

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal A$ and declare $W\subseteq|\mathcal A|$ open exactly when $|p|^{-1}(W)$ is open. Preimages preserve unions and finite intersections, so this defines a topology. Given a second such atlas $p\prime:U\prime\to\mathcal A$, form $Z=U\times_{\mathcal A}U\prime$ with projections $r:Z\to U$ and $s:Z\to U\prime$. The representable-diagonal result [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability], with schemes viewed as spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], says $Z$ is an algebraic space. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], both projections are smooth and surjective, hence flat and locally of finite presentation. They are continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] and open by [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open]. They are surjective on point sets by the field-extension lifting interpretation of surjectivity in the calculus node. All these assertions use the existing algebraic-space topology, with no topology on stack points presupposed.

source.place: Tag 04XL (lemma-topology-points), first paragraph: comparison of two presentations

proof.text: A continuous open surjection $h:E\to F$ reflects openness of subsets: if $h^{-1}(B)$ is open, then $B=h(h^{-1}(B))$ is open; the converse is continuity. Apply this to the two projections of step 2. The 2-isomorphism $pr\simeq p\prime s$ gives $|r|^{-1}(|p|^{-1}(W))=|s|^{-1}(|p\prime|^{-1}(W))$. Therefore $|p|^{-1}(W)$ is open if and only if this common preimage is open, if and only if $|p\prime|^{-1}(W)$ is open. The topology is independent of the atlas. Taking complements gives precisely the asserted closed-set criterion for every atlas. Together with step 1 this gives a surjective quotient map for every atlas.

Let $a:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be arbitrary. Choose scheme atlases $p:U\to\mathcal A$ and $q:V\to\mathcal B$. Regard $U$ as mapping to $\mathcal B$ by $ap$. The representable-diagonal result [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability] makes $Z=U\times_{\mathcal B}V$ an algebraic space, using [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Its projection $r:Z\to U$ is smooth and surjective by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], so it is continuous, open and surjective on points by that node, [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], and [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open]. Write $t:Z\to V$ for the other projection, which is continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. If $D$ is open in $|\mathcal B|$, then $|q|^{-1}(D)$ is open by the atlas criterion already proved. The equality $|r|^{-1}(|p|^{-1}(|a|^{-1}(D)))=|t|^{-1}(|q|^{-1}(D))$ shows the left side is open. Since $|r|$ is an open surjection, step 3 implies that $|p|^{-1}(|a|^{-1}(D))$ is open. The atlas criterion for $p$ now says $|a|^{-1}(D)$ is open. Thus every $|a|$ is continuous. This argument uses a fibre product of two schemes over $\mathcal B$, not an assumed scheme fibre product over a stack.

source.place: Tag 04XL (lemma-topology-points), continuity paragraph; its compatible-presentation argument performed before the optional etale scheme refinement

proof.text: For an algebraic space $A$ regarded as a stack, its point classes are exactly [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]: the fibre groupoids are discrete, so a 2-isomorphism is equality. Given any smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to A$, its map on the usual algebraic-space point spaces is continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], open by [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open], and surjective by step 1. Here smooth implies flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. It is therefore a quotient map by the two-line argument of step 3. Thus the topology defined in step 2 agrees with the usual etale-atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For a scheme use its identity as a smooth surjective atlas, viewing it as a space by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]; the identification of step 1 then makes the defining inverse-image condition exactly its Zariski topology. No quasi-compactness, separation, or finiteness assumption was used.

Step 1: well-definedness comes from whiskering, and atlas surjectivity from the field-extension lifting clause of lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus (the 04XI direction 2 to 1). Scheme points are identified with field classes through the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field. Step 2: Z=U×_A U' is an algebraic space by lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability. Both projections are base changes of smooth surjective atlases, so they are flat and locally of finite presentation. They are continuous by lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus, open by lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open with identity base change, and surjective on points. For a scheme, the space topology equals the Zariski topology by the flat-lfp node's statement that the topology is the quotient for any étale atlas. Step 3 is the elementary argument that an open surjection reflects open sets. Step 4 proves continuity through U×_B V, where r is the base change of q. This correctly replaces Stacks 04T1, and nothing is assumed about a. Step 5 identifies the topology with the usual one for spaces and schemes. Edge cases checked: empty stacks, the identity atlas of a scheme, an étale atlas of a space, nontrivial stabilizers, and a nonsmooth a. There is no cycle: I traversed the full closure. lean.statement: theorem stack_point_topology {S : Scheme.{u}} : (∀ (F : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)), IsAlgebraicModuliStack F → ∀ (U : Over S) (p : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) F), IsSmoothModuliAtlas F U p → Function.Surjective (moduliSchemePointMap p) ∧ ∀ D : Set (ModuliPoints F), IsClosed D ↔ IsClosed (moduliSchemePointMap p ⁻¹' D)) ∧ (∀ (F : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)) (G : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over S)), IsAlgebraicModuliStack F → IsAlgebraicModuliStack G → ∀ a : BasedFunctor F G, Continuous (moduliPointMap a)) ∧ (∀ A : AlgebraicSpace S, ∃ e : AlgebraicSpace.Point A.obj.obj ≃ₜ ModuliPoints (discreteModuli A.obj.obj), ∀ x : AlgebraicSpace.PointRepresentative A.obj.obj, e (Quot.mk _ x) = Quot.mk _ (moduliSpaceFieldObject x)) ∧ (∀ U : Over S, ∃ e : U.left ≃ₜ ModuliPoints (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)), ∀ x : U.left, e x = moduliSchemePointMap (BasedFunctor.id _) x)
